## Command Line Tools 

The command line interface is a text-based interface for interacting with programs on your computer. 
By contrast, we interact with many programs through a graphical user interface. 
For the course, you should get comfortable with command line interfaces. 
See this [short course](https://missing.csail.mit.edu/) for using the command line to run things on your computer. 

Programs like `pycharm` and `VS Code` give you a combination of a graphical user interface with a command line tool option, and are popular. 
However, they introduce an additional learning curve. 




### Windows 

See [this guide](https://docs.python.org/3/using/windows.html) or [this guide](https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tutorials/install-python-windows-10) to using `python` on Windows. 


## Packages

We use the following major packages in `python`: 

1. `numpy`: working with $n$-D arrays 
1. `mujoco` : Modeling and simulation of robotic systems
1. `matplotlib`: plotting

The following command uses `pip` to install these `python` packages 
```
pip install numpy mujoco matplotlib
```
If you want to use machine learning, consider the following packages:

1. `torch`: training of differentiable models 
1. `torchvision`: tools for vision models
1. `pandas`: working with data 
1. `tqdm`: progress bars in the command line 
1. `scikit-learn`: source some classic datasets



### Virtual Environment 

Virtual environments allow you to install a custom set of packages with custom package versions for a project. 

Inside the `robotics-course` directory, run
```
python -m venv code-venv
```
to create a blank virtual environment. 

Activate it, and then install packages. Upon activation, the command line prompt changes to start with the name of the virtual environment. Here, it would be `(code-venv)`:
```
source code-venv/bin/activate
pip install <packages above>
```

When you are done, you can run `deactivate` to return to the default global environment. 

## NumPy

A nice overview of using `numpy` is located [online here](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/user/absolute_beginners.html). 

Two **KEY** issues to watch out for: 

1. Standard matrix multiplication in `numpy` uses the `@` symbol, not the `*` symbol. Users coming from `Matlab` or `Julia` often trip over this issue a few times until they internalize the new symbol. 
1. 2D Arrays are stored in row-major form. 


## MuJoCo

### Drag-and-Drop Mode 

Open a terminal window (command window - `cmd` on Windows) and run 

```python
python3 -m mujoco.viewer
```

This command should open a window with nothing visible yet. You can drag `xml` files describing a `MuJoCo` environment and it will show up. The `xml` needs to be self-contained or use complete paths to subfiles. 

### Usage Example: Simulation

Once you have installed `mujoco` in `python`, you can run [this code](code/basic_mujoco.py) by running this command in the command line from the root of this repository:

```
python3 code/basic_mujoco.py
```
